MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  DECEMBER 1, 2020

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Addleman, Arata, Bayer, Buresh, Carman,
  Carrese,  Corman,  *Schmitz,  Shinn,
  Seamans, Stegura, Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Medawar, Silvano

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Principal Community Planner, Michael Baker
  International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

NONE

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CITYWIDE LAND USE - LAND USE ALTERNATIVES DISCUSSION

John Bellas, MBI stated that at the last meeting recommendations were discussed for the Land
Use Element, and introduced Dan Wery, MBI to provide the presentation on land use alternatives.

Mr. Wery provided and overview on the direction received from earlier meetings, which include:

  •  Maintain rural character and scenic views
  •  Acknowledge market dynamics
  •  Adress RHNA – higher density / mixed-use in Commercial District; Allow for ADUs; Staff
  housing (school properties)
  •  Focus on opportunities for infill / redevelopment
  •  Promote park and recreation in 5-minute walking distance

Mr. Wery began the discussion by asking if there is a need to change the current density of 22
unites per acre; should increasing the density be considered; and, should no net loss / limited loss
of non-residential be considered.

Mr. Wery stated that one of the changes that needs to be made to the mixed use overlay zone is
to remove the Pepper Tree Lane site; that area has already been developed for high density
residential.

Mr. Wery stated that potential growth and development opportunities are in the Commercial
District. He noted the areas where there is the most opportunities for change in the next five to
twenty years, which include: the entrance to Norris Drive, the Promenade Mall, Bart Earle Way;
the central court area at the church property, and the Brick Walk property.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES,DECEMBER 1, 2020
 Mr. Wery provided a slide showing that based on existing or recent developments, a Residual
Land Value (RLV) of $100 per sq. ft. with 20% affordable housing is necessary for a project to be
feasible in the Commercial District. From there, they looked at what it would take for the market
to produce the city’s housing obligations. In order to be in the RLV range of $100 per sq. ft. or
more, the city would need to allow for 50 to 60 dwelling units per acre including a 40% density
bonus.

Director Wahba noted that the city’s current 22 dwelling units per acre does not include the 40%
density bonus, which would take it to 30 dwelling units per acre. Mr. Wery added that 20% would
be affordable housing units.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked how many housing units are required for the city under
RHNA and will the number be satisfied only in the mixed use Commercial District. Mr. Wery stated
that because of the density needed to meet the city’s RHNA obligations, the city needs to meet
the State requirement under the Housing Community Development (HCD) Department, which
requires 22 dwelling units per acre in order to consider qualifying to meet their lower income units.
Some credits can come from Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) or if someone came in and
subsidized low-income housing and these must be documented as low income housing in order
to qualify. Ms. Barbyaya stated the the RHNA requirement is 191 units. Ms. Barbhaya stated that
institutonal properties are being looked at in order to meet these numbers as well.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN inquired about the current number of dwelling units per acre
in residential developments in the city’s Commercial District. Ms. Barbhaya stated that for the
mixed use overlay, it is 22 units per acre, however, for high density residential it is 8 units per
acre. Director Wahba added that the Las Colinas project at 627 Deep Valley Drive was built at 40
dwelling units per acre.

Mr. Wery provided examples of various properties that have 40 to 50 units per acres. All the
properties have some commercial space. The suggestion is not to measure by dwelling units per
acre and instead to use Floor Area Ratio (FAR) so the size can be controlled.

Mr. Wery provided a summary of recommended changes to the mixed use overlay zone with the
purpose of allowing future development to occur. These recommendations include the following:

  •  Increase base residential density from 22 to 30 dwelling units per acre
  •  Create community benefit density bonus program
  o Up to 60 dwelling units per acre
  •  Additional Affordable Housing Density Bonus

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked since the La Colinas project was built at 40 units
per acre, why wasn’t 40 units per acre used as the threshold for economic viability. Mr. Wery
stated that Las Colinas was used as a benchmark and the project was built at 40 units per acre
with no affordable housing.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested concentrating higher density development at
specific spaces where there could be community benefit for the city as opposed to having
unplanned developments throughout the Commercial District. Mr. Wery stated that there are tools
where the commercial base could be protected.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS expressed her concern with the detoriation of the buildings
along Silver Spur and is not sure that this is being addressed. She also stated that she did not
care for the previous slides showing “cut-throughs” in the Promenade area. Ms. Seamans
suggested to look on a smaller scale to improve the area to draw people to the Commercial
District.

Mr. Wery provided a summary of recommended changes to the mixed use overlay zone with the
development standards in particular. These recommendations include the following:

  •  Maintain minimum lot size – 1 acre
  •  Increase lot coverage from 40% to ± 60%
  •  Increase height from 3 stories/44 ft. to 4 stories/54’
  •  Reduce total maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR) from 3.0 to 2.5
  •  Retain non-residential: minimum percentage; no/limited net loss

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES,DECEMBER 1, 2020
 Mr. Wery provided a summary of the items that were discussed at this and previous meetings,
which included:

  •  Remove Mixed Use Overlay Zone (MUOZ) from the Pepper Tree Lane site
  •  Update MUOZ standards based on market study, and traffic impacts
  •  Consider updating parking requirements for efficient land use
  •  Consider Form-based Code / revised development standards
  •  Consider incentives for community benefits

COMMITTEE CORMAN complimented MBI on providing an overall vision/strategy of what the
community should represent.

CHAIR SCHMITZ concurred and stated that it is important to note comments that committee
members have made and hope that those comments are incorporated. CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked
MBI and the Committee for their commitment and time dedicated to the City.
Mr. Bellas thanked Director Wahba and Planning Manager Naughton for all of their work,

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS / FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

Ms. Barbhaya provided an overview of the next steps, including the next meeting which will be on
the Sustainability Element. In January there will be a meeting on Mobility; in February the Housing
Element will be discussed; and, from then on the Housing Element will be drafted and meetings
will be held prior to being submitted to HCD.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee and adjourned the meeting at 8:06 p.m.

The next General Plan Advisory Committee meeting will be held on Tuesday, December 15, 2020
at 6:00 p.m. via Video Teleconference.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

____________________________________  _____________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
